newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to issue T$8.0 bln in NCDs on Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to issue T$8.0 bln in NCDs on Tuesday.

text.p: Taiwan's central bank said on Tuesday it would issue T$8 billion in one-month negotiable certificates of deposit later in the day.
Bids would close at 3.00 pm (0700 GMT), a central bank official said.

Central bank deputy governor Hsu Chia-tung said on Monday the bank would continue to tighten liquidity in an apparent effort to cool the red-hot stock market -- despite persistently high short-term interest rates.
Hsu said after markets close that recent interest rates hikes reflected a stock market rally that as of Monday had seen the Taiwan share index rise 23.5 percent in 1997 alone.

"The central bank cannot intervene as to where the funds flow, but it will continue to observe and adjust the situation," Hsu said, indicating the bank would continue to issue NCDs to mop up banking system liquidity.
"We will control the quantity (of funds)," Hsu said, adding the central bank could tolerate higher interest rates.
The central bank had repeatedly issued NCDs in recent sessions in a strategy widely seen as aiming to cool down the sizzling stock market.

The overnight interbank rate ended at 6.081 percent on Monday, with 30-day short-term commercial paper at 6.00, lower than in recent sessions but still well above the central bank's target zone of 5.00-5.50 percent.
On Monday, share prices surged past 8,400 points to yet another six-year high on huge turnover of T$176.88 billion.
